title: Interim Study of Procedures for Investigating the Effect of Light on Impression and Behavior

findings.antecedent: variations in environmental lighting (six distinct arrangements)
findings.consequent: initial ratings on 17 of 34 Semantic Differential rating scales
findings.mechanism: Lighting variations alter the overall impression of the physical space.
findings.quote: 17 (of 34) rating scales showed a significant difference in response to the room under the six lighting arrangements.

findings.consequent: impression on all 34 Semantic Differential rating scales (comparative ratings)
findings.mechanism: Providing a frame of reference (comparative ratings) enhanced the effectiveness of rating scales without altering basic judgments.
findings.quote: all of the 34 rating scales showed a significant difference in impression between two or more of the six lighting arrangements

findings.consequent: general EVALUATIVE IMPRESSION (Factor 1 from SD analysis)
findings.mechanism: Arrangements 6 and 4 were generally most preferred, while 3 and 5 were least preferred.
findings.quote: Factor 1 was a general EVALUATIVE IMPRESSION

findings.consequent: PERCEPTUAL CLARITY impression (Factor 2 from SD analysis)
findings.mechanism: Arrangements 5 and 6 were perceived as clearest/brightest, while 1, 2, 3, and 4 had lesser photic energy.
findings.quote: Factor 2 appeared to represent an impression that is tentatively named PERCEPTUAL CLARITY

findings.consequent: SPATIAL COMPLEXITY impression (Factor 3 from SD analysis)
findings.mechanism: Changes in lighting arrangement did not significantly affect this impression.
findings.quote: changes in lighting arrangement did not significantly affect impression in this case.

findings.mechanism: Arrangements 1 and 3 were judged significantly less spacious than arrangements 6 and 2.
findings.quote: Factor 4 was an impression of SPACIOUSNESS. Lighting arrangements 1 and 3 were judged significantly less spacious

findings.mechanism: This factor did not strongly differentiate between the six lighting arrangements.
findings.quote: this factor did not strongly differentiate between the six lighting arrangements

findings.antecedent: change in intensity of horizontal illumination from overhead diffusing system (10 fc vs 100 fc, arrangements 3 vs 5)
findings.mechanism: Changing only light intensity had a negligible effect on general 'evaluative impressions'.
findings.quote: changing only light intensity had a negligible effect on general 'evaluative impressions.'

findings.antecedent: change in intensity of horizontal illumination from overhead diffusing system (10 fc vs 100 fc, arrangements 3 vs 5)
findings.mechanism: Higher intensity system (arrangement 5) was rated as most clear, bright, and distinct, while arrangement 3 was at the opposite extreme.
findings.quote: impressions of arrangements 3 and 5 varied widely for 'perceptual clarity.'

findings.mechanism: Higher brightness levels tended to produce an impression of increased 'spaciousness'.
findings.quote: higher brightness levels tended to produce an impression of increased 'spaciousness.'

findings.antecedent: change in distribution characteristics from an overhead lighting system (downlighting vs diffuse, arrangements 1 vs 3, both at 10 fc)
findings.mechanism: Arrangements 1 and 3 produced a roughly similar impression regarding 'perceptual clarity'.
findings.quote: arrangements 1 and 3... produced a roughly similar impression regarding 'perceptual clarity;'

findings.antecedent: change in distribution characteristics from an overhead lighting system (downlighting vs diffuse, arrangements 1 vs 3, both at 10 fc)
findings.mechanism: Arrangement 1 (downlighting) consistently produced more positive 'evaluative impressions' than arrangement 3.
findings.quote: arrangement 1 (downlighting) consistently produced more positive 'evaluative impressions' than arrangement 3.

findings.antecedent: change in distribution characteristics from an overhead lighting system (downlighting vs diffuse, arrangements 1 vs 3, both at 10 fc)
findings.mechanism: There were marginally significant differences in the impression of 'spaciousness'.
findings.quote: There were also marginally significant differences in the impression of 'spaciousness.'

findings.antecedent: addition of limited wall lighting to a low intensity overhead lighting system (arrangement 4 vs 1)
findings.mechanism: Arrangement 4 (downlights plus wall lights) was consistently evaluated more positively than arrangement 1 (downlights only).
findings.quote: arrangement 4 (downlights plus wall lights) was consistently evaluated more positively than arrangement 1 (downlights only).

findings.antecedent: addition of limited wall lighting to a low intensity overhead lighting system (arrangement 4 vs 1)
findings.mechanism: The limited wall lighting improved 'perceptual clarity' somewhat.
findings.quote: The limited wall lighting also improved 'perceptual clarity' somewhat

findings.antecedent: addition of limited wall lighting to a low intensity overhead lighting system (arrangement 4 vs 1)
findings.mechanism: The limited wall lighting significantly affected the impression of 'spaciousness'.
findings.quote: and significantly affected the impression of 'spaciousness.'

findings.consequent: judgments of similarity and difference (MDS analysis)
findings.mechanism: A three-dimensional perceptual solution (peripheral/overhead, uniform/non-uniform, bright-dim) best accounted for the data.
findings.quote: a three-dimensional perceptual solution best accounted for the judgments of similarity and difference.

findings.mechanism: Both procedures yielded essentially equivalent results for this aspect of visual experience.
findings.quote: A correlation of 0.99 between the perceptual clarity SD ratings and the 'bright/dim' INDSCAL dimension was achieved

findings.mechanism: Evaluative impressions are correlated with the 'overhead/peripheral' dimension.
findings.quote: A correlation of 0.83 with the 'overhead/peripheral' dimension was obtained in the first step

findings.mechanism: These two dimensions are strong predictors of evaluative impressions.
findings.quote: a correlation of 0.92 was achieved in the second step, using both the 'overhead/peripheral' and 'uniform/non-uniform' dimensions as predictors

findings.mechanism: Evaluative impressions are adequately represented as a linear combination of these three dimensions.
findings.quote: The addition of the 'bright/dim' dimension contributed little additional explanatory power-only increasing the correlation to 0.94.

findings.mechanism: Spaciousness impressions are correlated with the 'uniform/non-uniform' dimension.
findings.quote: A correlation of 0.69 with the 'uniform/non-uniform' dimension was obtained in the first step

findings.mechanism: These two dimensions are strong predictors of spaciousness impressions.
findings.quote: a correlation of 0.94 was obtained in the second step, using both the 'uniform/non-uniform' and 'overhead/peripheral' dimensions as predictors

findings.mechanism: Spaciousness impressions are well-represented as a linear combination of all three dimensions.
findings.quote: The addition of the 'bright-dim' dimension as a predictor increased the multiple regression coefficient to 0.98.

findings.consequent: negative evaluative judgments and reduced levels of social interaction (overt gestures)
findings.mechanism: Subjects tended to reduce overt gestures from subjects seated at the conference table, suggesting less social interaction.
findings.quote: diffuse overhead lighting arrangements 3 and 5 elicited generally negative evaluative judgments on the rating scales.

findings.consequent: more positive evaluative judgments and increased levels of social interaction (overt gestures)
findings.mechanism: Subjects were observed to make more overt gestures, such as 'very flattering' or 'relaxed', indicating increased social interaction.
findings.quote: overhead downlighting arrangements 1 and 4 elicited more positive evaluative judgments

findings.antecedent: modified lighting arrangement (coffee-bar illuminated, rest of room unlighted except for stray light, drapery drawn, wall-lighting on major interior wall opposite entrance)
findings.consequent: seat selection pattern (facing interior of room, generally toward the light)
findings.mechanism: Users seemed to turn their backs on the entrance area, confirming that lighting conditions may induce instinctive or learned tendencies in overt behavior.
findings.quote: With this second lighting condition, most users who had a choice in their seat selection seemed to turn their backs on the entrance area

findings.antecedent: initial lighting condition (coffee-bar illuminated, tables/room unlighted except for stray light, drapery drawn, wall-lighting on major interior wall opposite entrance)
findings.consequent: seat selection pattern (facing entrance stair, a center of activity)
findings.mechanism: A distinct tendency for those first selecting seats at each table to face the entrance stair, which was a center of activity.
findings.quote: There was a distinct tendency for those first selecting their seats at each table to face the entrance stair, which was a center of activity

stimuli.description: Six different lighting arrangements in a medium-sized conference room at the General Electric Lighting Institute at Nela Park. Arrangements included: 1) Overhead Downlighting, Low Intensity; 2) Peripheral Wall-Lighting, All Walls; 3) Overhead Diffuse, Low Setting; 4) Combination: Overhead Downlighting (1) + End Walls; 5) Overhead Diffuse, High Intensity; 6) Combination: Overhead Downlighting (1) + Peripheral (2) + Overhead Diffuse (3).

tables.description: Factor loadings for five Semantic Differential factors: Evaluative, Perceptual Clarity, Spatial Complexity, Spaciousness, and Formality.
key_stats: Factor 1 (Evaluative) loadings: Friendly (.89), Pleasant (.89), Like (.86), Harmony (.83), Satisfying (.83), Beautiful (.83), Sociable (.83), Relaxed (.83), Interesting (.81)
Factor 2 (Perceptual Clarity) loadings: Clear (.86), Bright (.84), Faces Clear (.77), Distinct (.77), Focused (.71), Radiant (.61)

limitations: Findings are tentative, representing limited samples of lighting variables.
The study is an interim report, suggesting further work is needed for confirmation.
